title: Linearization of Quadrature Digital Power Amplifiers by Neural Network of ULR_LSTM: Unsupervised Learning Residual LSTM
problem: Digital power amplifiers suffer from nonlinearity requiring complex predistortion. State-of-the-art digital predistortion methods rely on iterative learning control, creating high computational complexity and extensive training overhead.
motivation: Existing ILC-based predistortion is computationally expensive and slow to train; faster, simpler alternatives are needed for practical RF/wireless deployment.
method: Unsupervised Learning Residual LSTM (ULR_LSTM) performs behavioral modeling of the DPA without iterative learning control; DPD model is obtained via inverse training process. Implemented as a 15-bit transformer-based quadrature DPA chip in 28nm CMOS with Class-G and IQ-cell-sharing techniques.
key_novelty: First unsupervised LSTM-based approach for digital predistortion, eliminating iterative learning control entirely.
contributions: ULR_LSTM neural network for DPA behavioral modeling without ILC
Inverse training methodology to derive DPD from behavioral model
15-bit transformer-based quadrature DPA chip in 28nm CMOS
Error vector magnitude of -40.4dB for 802.11ax 40MHz 64QAM signals
baselines: Prior DPD methods using iterative learning control
limitations: Evaluation limited to single signal format (802.11ax); generalization to other wireless standards and modulations not demonstrated.
primary_theme: Neural network-based digital predistortion for RF power amplifiers
